newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Polyta says mulls merger with supplier.
newsitem.headline: Polyta says mulls merger with supplier.

text.p: Indonesian petrochemical giant PT Tri Polyta Indonesia said on Thursday it was studying the possibility of a merger with its main raw material supplier PT Chandra Asri in a bid to boost performance.
"The matter (for a possible merger) is being studied.. but no decision has been made yet," vice president commissioner Peter Gontha told a news conference.
Tri Polyta, also listed in New York, produces polypropylene, a type of plastic used to manufacture a wide range of consumer products such as carpets, rope and automobile parts.
Gontha declined to give further details of the possible merger with Chandra Asri, a producer of propylene which is the raw material for polypropylene. Chandra Asri is an affiliate of Tri Polyta.
Gontha, however, said mergers between upstream and downstream petrochemical companies were sometimes done to limit risk amid sharp price fluctuations in the international market.
He said propylene prices in Southeast Asia hd risen sharply to $680 to $700 per tonne currently from $380-$400 in the same period last year.
Chandra Asri currently supplies some 240,000 tonnes of propylene per year to Tri Polyta which needs some 360,000 tonnes annually, Gontha said.
Tri Polyta posted a net profit of 26 billion rupiah in 1996, down sharply from 58.52 billion rupiah in 1995.
